page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine configured with 64 vCPUs and 432.0 GB of RAM, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, this instance features 32 physical cores operating at 2.6 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware allocation is dedicated, providing a 35 MB L3 cache and support for advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA.

For storage, the E64s_v3 includes a local 885 GB SSD and is Premium Storage capable, allowing integration with high-performance external disks. In terms of performance, benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, scoring in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench. However, multi-core execution is more robust, achieving average ratings in stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests, alongside strong performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and extended instruction tests.

Memory bandwidth for both read and write operations remains in the average tier, supporting steady data throughput. This resource density makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without needing top-tier single-thread compute speeds. The E64s_v3 is configured for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, multi-threaded data processing, and enterprise application backends.
description: Microsoft Azure E64s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 432.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor at 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, it includes an 885 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage. While single-core benchmark results are weak, its multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are average, with strong results in multi-threaded decompression and extended instructions. Lacking a GPU, this instance is optimized for memory-heavy workloads rather than raw single-threaded compute or graphics acceleration. It is best suited for databases, enterprise applications, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
